# retry

<link-summary>Calls a function again when it throws, with a growing wait between attempts.</link-summary>

<web-summary>retry() — Calls a function again when it throws, with a growing wait between attempts. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/function</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function retry<T>(fn: (attempt: number) => T, options: RetryOptions = {}): T;
```

The wait starts at `delay`, is multiplied by `multiplier` after each failure and never exceeds `maxDelay`. `shouldRetry` decides whether a given failure is worth repeating at all — a rate limit usually is, a bad argument never is.

The function receives the attempt number, starting at `1`. When the last attempt fails its error is thrown on. The wait itself goes through `sleep`, which defaults to `Utilities.sleep` where that exists and can be replaced in a test.

## Parameters

| Parameter                     | Type                     | Description                                                               |
| :---------------------------- | :----------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `fn`                          | `(attempt: number) => T` | The function to call. It receives the attempt number.                     |
| `options` _(optional)_ `= {}` | `RetryOptions`           | `attempts`, `delay`, `multiplier`, `maxDelay`, `shouldRetry` and `sleep`. |

## Returns

`T` — whatever the function returns on the attempt that succeeds.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition                                                           |
| :------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the first argument is not a function, or an option is out of range. |

## Examples

### Retrying a flaky call

```javascript
const response = retry(() => UrlFetchApp.fetch(url), {
  attempts: 4,
  delay: 500,
  multiplier: 2,
  shouldRetry: (error) => String(error).includes("429")
});
```
